---
title: Tool versions
description: Check explicit commands and minimum numeric versions without installing or repairing tools.
---

# Tool versions

Input `tools` lists `command`, `args` and `minimumVersion`; optional
`checkTimeoutMs` defaults to 5000 (100–300000). Commands run without a shell.
The host must allow subprocess creation. Versions are dot-separated decimal
numbers, compared numerically; the first recognizable output version is used.
The result is `{pass:true}` or only failing `target`, `code`, `actual` entries.
`target` is the command and `actual` is the parsed version or null.

Problems: [missing](problems/tool-missing.md),
[unusable](problems/tool-unusable.md),
[unparseable](problems/version-unparseable.md),
[too old](problems/tool-version.md).
Timeout, output overflow, unexpected launch errors and cleanup failures are
execution faults, not problems. Cancellation propagates after physical process
cleanup. No installation or repair is performed.

---
title: Tool version too old
description: The parsed tool version is below the requested minimum version.
---

`target` is the command; `actual` is its parsed numeric version. Compare the
requested minimum, select a suitable executable or upgrade separately.
The check performs no upgrade. See [tool checks](../check.md).

---
title: Directory access
description: Check absolute directory paths and explicit exists, read or write requirements.
---

# Directory access

Input `directories` lists absolute `path` and nonempty `requirements` from
`exists`, `read`, `write`. Symlinks are not accepted as directories.
Read uses host access checks. Write creates an exclusive probe file, reads it
back and deletes it in `finally`; it does not modify existing files.
The Engine host must have the requested permissions.

Results contain only failures: [not-directory](problems/not-directory.md) or
[directory-unusable](problems/directory-unusable.md). `target` is the absolute
path; `actual` is the filesystem error code or null. Invalid input, unexpected
filesystem errors, readback mismatch and cleanup errors remain execution
faults. Cancellation propagates after probe cleanup. No repair is performed.

---
title: Directory access
description: Check absolute directory paths and explicit exists, read or write requirements.
---

# Directory access

Input `directories` lists absolute `path` and nonempty `requirements` from
`exists`, `read`, `write`. Symlinks are not accepted as directories.
Read uses host access checks. Write creates an exclusive probe file, reads it
back and deletes it in `finally`; it does not modify existing files.
The Engine host must have the requested permissions.

Results contain only failures: [not-directory](problems/not-directory.md) or
[directory-unusable](problems/directory-unusable.md). `target` is the absolute
path; `actual` is the filesystem error code or null. Invalid input, unexpected
filesystem errors, readback mismatch and cleanup errors remain execution
faults. Cancellation propagates after probe cleanup. No repair is performed.

---
title: Directory unavailable
description: The directory is missing or requested access failed with a recognized filesystem error.
---

`target` is the absolute directory path; `actual` is ENOENT, ENOTDIR, EACCES,
EPERM, EROFS, ENOSPC or EDQUOT. Check path, permissions, filesystem capacity and
mount state. Resolve the cause separately; no repair is attempted.
Unexpected errors and cleanup failures are faults, not this problem.
See [directory checks](../check.md).

---
title: Network reachability
description: Check explicit DNS names and HTTP status expectations with bounded resource lifetimes.
---

# Network reachability

Input contains `dns` names and `http` entries with `url`, `expectedStatus`,
`followRedirects`; at least one check is required. Optional `checkTimeoutMs`
defaults to 5000 (100–300000). The host requires DNS/network access and Node
subprocess support. HTTP(S) URLs cannot contain credentials.
DNS runs in a bounded subprocess; HTTP response bodies are cancelled.

Problems: [DNS unavailable](problems/dns-unavailable.md),
[unexpected HTTP status](problems/http-status.md),
[HTTP unavailable](problems/http-unavailable.md).
Results contain only failures; `target` is the DNS name or URL, `actual` is
the DNS error/address, status string or fetch diagnostic.
Timeouts, invalid inputs, unexpected subprocess faults and cleanup failures
remain execution faults. Cancellation propagates and physical resources are
released. This is a point-in-time probe, not a network repair or guarantee.

---
title: Network reachability
description: Check explicit DNS names and HTTP status expectations with bounded resource lifetimes.
---

# Network reachability

Input contains `dns` names and `http` entries with `url`, `expectedStatus`,

Timeouts, invalid inputs, unexpected subprocess faults and cleanup failures

released. This is a point-in-time probe, not a network repair or guarantee.

---
title: Unexpected HTTP status
description: The HTTP response did not satisfy status and redirect expectations.
---

`target` is the requested URL; `actual` is the decimal response status.
Check expectedStatus and followRedirects, endpoint health and authentication.
A redirect fails when following redirects is disabled, even when listed as an
expected status. See [network checks](../check.md).
